DRIFT FOUND (literal step set between tests/scored/functional/prompt.md and tests/scored/functional/judge.toml): protocol R (prompt.md:45) says 'As Aud Halvorsen (Observer) and as Tomas Varga (candidate) ... replay one observed move, one add-candidate and one note request.' -- three request kinds. The criteria that grade that exact protocol require four: hro_observer_readonly (judge.toml:172-173) 'replays in the Observer's session of an observed move, add-candidate, open-job and note request are each refused' and hro_candidate_no_staff (judge.toml:181-182) 'replays in a candidate's session of an observed move, add-candidate, open-job and note request are each refused'. No protocol step tells the judge to replay an open-job request in the Observer's or candidate's session (protocol N only does it for Ingrid). The same scenario is therefore described with different request sets in the two files.
counterexample: Weak app passing: an app that refuses Observer/candidate moves, add-candidate and notes but lets an Observer (or candidate) session POST a new job. A judge that executes protocol R literally replays only move, add-candidate and note, sees all three refused, and can award hro_observer_readonly / hro_candidate_no_staff (weight 1 each) despite the open-job write going through. Conforming app failing: a correct app whose Observer UI offers no open-job control; a judge that follows protocol R never captures/replays the open-job request, so 'each of move, add-candidate, open-job and note ... refused' is not observed and a strict batched judge may give binary 0 for unobserved evidence on either row. Either way the score depends on which file the judge treats as authoritative.
suggested_fix: Make protocol R in tests/scored/functional/prompt.md say 'replay one observed move, one add-candidate, one open-job and one note request' for the Observer and the candidate (or drop open-job from both criteria), so the prompt and both criteria list the same request set.
